It enforces spatial smoothness and piecewise-constant structures by penalizing the magnitude of gradients between neighboring voxels [S2].

The evidence explicitly states that the method regularizes the total variation of predicted density values to ensure 'compact, smooth geometry'. The mathematical definition provided for the Total Variation loss ($L_{TV}$) involves the square root of the sum of squared differences between neighboring voxels in x, y, and z directions ($|V|^{-1} sum sqrt(Delta^2_x + Delta^2_y + Delta^2_z)$). In the context of discrete grids like voxels, these differences represent the gradients between neighboring voxels. Penalizing the magnitude of these gradients (the L1 norm of the gradient vector, approximated here) is the standard definition of Total Variation regularization, which is known to enforce piecewise-constant structures and spatial smoothness. Therefore, the claim accurately reflects the mechanism described in the evidence.
